clue.text: Run through composition without introduction of reeds

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of outside, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: a piece is a musical or written composition

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so only the first letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of reeds

explanation.surface: A musician playing a work for wind band without the reed section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, not lacking: the composition goes around the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce something is to stab or pass a blade right through it.

clue.text: A breach in a leaf of the family tree

indicators.note: the first part is placed inside the second

parts.note: a leaf of a book is a page
a rent is a tear or breach
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tear in a page of a family history chart.
explanation.definitionFit: Parentage is one's descent from particular parents, the lineage a family tree records.

clue.text: He's left the company and demands payment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a former member of a theatre company

definitions.note: with 'He' shared, one who demands payment
definitions.meaning: second meaning: one who insists on what is owed

explanation.surface: A departing employee insisting on being paid off.
explanation.walkthrough: The company is a troupe of players, so someone who has left is a former actor.
explanation.definitionFit: An exactor is one who extorts or insists on dues, taxes or money owed.

clue.text: Cockney friend catches cold wrap him in this warm covering?

indicators.note: catching something takes it inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate
a chill is a cold

explanation.surface: A Londoner's mate has a cold, so bundle him up in something cosy.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys are working-class East Londoners known for rhyming slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinchilla fur is famously soft and dense, made into coats and wraps for warmth.

clue.text: Loaded volatile new fuel in rear

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed inside the following word
something volatile is unstable and liable to change, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: N for new plus the four letters of fuel, rearranged
aft is the rear part of a ship

explanation.surface: A tanker at the back of a ship freshly filled with explosive fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaded' and 'volatile fuel' suggest a cargo, but loaded is slang for rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is informal for having plenty of money, so wealthy people are affluent.

clue.text: Unrestrained infantry suffer defeat, securing nothing

parts.note: foot soldiers are the infantry

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so one word encloses another

parts.note: to lose is to suffer defeat
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Foot soldiers beaten in a battle that gained no ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Footloose means free of ties or responsibilities, able to go anywhere.

clue.text: A record tip

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a written roll of items
second meaning: to lean over, as a ship does

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a tip-off for a record, but the meanings are separate.
explanation.definitionFit: A list is a catalogue of entries, and to list is to heel or tilt to one side.

clue.text: Serious money in deposit

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a sum paid in advance to seal a bargain

explanation.surface: Someone talking about a serious sum of money paid into the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means grave and sincere, and as a noun it is a pledge sum paid down.

clue.text: Some light reading in the flight

definitions.note: a step forming part of a flight of stairs

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken

parts.note: running across the two words

explanation.surface: Taking some easy reading material on an aeroplane journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The flight looks like an air journey; it is a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: A tread is the horizontal surface of a stair step, one of many in a flight.

clue.text: Girl losing head in song

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: Maria is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman so lost in her singing that she is carried away.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera or oratorio.

clue.text: Better prepared for study? That's right

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
i.e., Latin id est, means that is
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A student asking whether extra study makes them better prepared, and being told yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready means prepared, and its comparative form describes someone more fully prepared.

clue.text: Abide by notice

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to keep or follow a rule or custom
second meaning: to see or perceive

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it sounds like obeying a posted notice; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb covers both following a law or custom and perceiving something with the eyes.

clue.text: Diamonds worn by celebrity well in evidence

indicators.note: jewels worn by a person sit on them, so one word is set within the other

parts.note: a notable is a famous or important person
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A film star wearing diamonds that everyone can plainly see.
explanation.definitionFit: Something well in evidence is plainly visible, easily spotted by anyone looking.

clue.text: Animal back in the long grass

indicators.note: going back means the animal's name is read from its end

parts.note: a deer is a common crossword animal

explanation.surface: A creature heading back into the tall grass to hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeds are tall stiff grasses that grow in wet ground beside rivers and marshes.

clue.text: Heartless potentate sent lice to spread plague

indicators.note: with the heart gone only the outermost letters remain

parts.note: first and last letters of potentate

indicators.note: spreading scatters things about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: A cruel ruler unleashing lice to spread disease among his people.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestilence is a deadly epidemic disease, a plague in the old biblical sense.

clue.text: High level transport by rail, fit for commuting

indicators.note: to commute is to exchange or interchange, so the letters swap places

parts.note: the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: A rail service deemed suitable for daily commuters.
explanation.walkthrough: Commuting looks like travel to work, but its older sense is exchanging, which signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An airlift carries people or supplies by aircraft, so it is transport high in the sky.

clue.text: Tool for getting in can undo entrances to every room

parts.note: a tin is a can
to undo a door or package is to open it

indicators.note: an entrance is the way in, so the first letters of the following words are taken

parts.note: the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A burglar's skeleton key that unlocks the doors to every room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting in' suggests breaking into a house; the tool gets into a can.
explanation.definitionFit: A can opener cuts into the lid of a tin, so it is the tool for getting at the contents.

clue.text: Excel in public work

parts.note: overt means open, done in public view
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone shining in a job for the public sector.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtop is to rise above or surpass, which is what excelling over others means.

clue.text: Correspondent in enclosure accompanied by Society member

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
a Friend is a member of the Religious Society of Friends, a Quaker

explanation.surface: A letter writer inside a compound alongside a club member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accompanied by' simply places one piece next to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen friend is someone you know mainly through exchanging letters, a regular correspondent.

clue.text: Long time hero put in shade

indicators.note: one word is put inside the other

parts.note: an eon is an immensely long period
an idol is a hero who is worshipped

explanation.surface: A long-time hero eclipsed, put in the shade by someone newer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in shade' looks like a phrase meaning outshone, but shade stands alone as the definition: a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade is a ghost or spirit, and an eidolon is a phantom or spectral image.

clue.text: Find fault with student entry and turn away

indicators.note: an entry goes into something, so one letter is put inside the word

parts.note: a defect is a fault
L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A teacher criticising a pupil's work and then dismissing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Find fault with' looks like one verb meaning criticise; fault alone supplies the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflect something is to make it change course, to turn it aside.

clue.text: Join passengers in Orient express, say about noon

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the combined words go around a letter

parts.note: the Orient is the East, E
an express is one kind of train, as 'say' shows
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: Boarding the famous Orient Express around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: The Orient Express looks like one name, but the words split: Orient for East, express as an example of a train.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrain is to board a train, so one joins the other travellers in the carriages.

clue.text: Motivate one getting uptight inside

indicators.note: getting something inside means one word takes in another, as 'inside' confirms

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: the word splits as up plus tight, and taut means tight

explanation.surface: Spurring on someone who is tense and nervous inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uptight' looks like one word for tense, but it splits into a reversal signal and a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To actuate is to move someone to act, to motivate or prompt them.

clue.text: Humid environment needed for fine threads

indicators.note: an environment surrounds whatever lives in it, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: humid air is damp or wet
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Damp conditions being necessary for spinning delicate threads.
explanation.definitionFit: The weft is the set of crosswise threads woven through the warp on a loom.

clue.text: Rolled around, being hurt

definitions.meaning: first meaning: past tense of wind, as with thread round a spool

explanation.surface: Someone tumbling about on the ground after an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are pronounced differently, rhyming with round and with swooned.
explanation.definitionFit: Thread is wound round a reel, and a wound is an injury to the body.

clue.text: Cryptic clue associated with a sport for a gambler

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling and hidden, so the letters are disguised by rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crossword clue about a sport, written for punters.
explanation.definitionFit: A speculator takes risky positions hoping to profit, gambling on markets or prices.

clue.text: Youngster left in bed

indicators.note: one letter goes inside the following word

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A child left alone in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a human child; the youngster is a young horse, or a junior sports player.
explanation.definitionFit: A colt is a young male horse, and also a young or junior player in sport.

clue.text: Bring fellow going to eat out

indicators.note: something going leaves, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: to fetch is to go and bring
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: Inviting a friend along to dine at a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat out' suggests a restaurant meal; here it means corrode.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid etches metal by corroding it, eating away the surface to leave a design.

clue.text: Left on the board victorious, though losing bishop

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped out of the word

parts.note: an unbeaten side has won every game
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A chess player who has won but given up a bishop that stays off the board.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture makes 'board' a chessboard; here it is the old sense of a dining table.
explanation.definitionFit: Food left on the board, the table, is food nobody has consumed.

clue.text: Wounded eagle in descent

indicators.note: a wounded thing is damaged and misshapen, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: An injured eagle coming down from the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Descent' suggests a bird falling; here it means ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Descent is ancestry, the line of forebears from whom a person is born.

clue.text: Farm workers possibly leaving us in the lurch

definitions.meaning: first meaning: labourers who dig and clear drainage channels

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for those who do this, signalled by 'possibly'
definitions.meaning: second meaning: people who abandon us, from the slang verb to ditch

explanation.surface: Farmhands walking off the job and leaving us stranded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' admits the second reading is a playful one: anyone who ditches others could be called this.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditchers dig and maintain field drains, and to ditch someone is to abandon them.

clue.text: Take command to cut off capital

definitions.note: read as two words, be head
definitions.meaning: first meaning, split into two words: to be the head, the one in charge
second meaning: to remove someone's head, capital being an old word for it

explanation.surface: Seizing power in order to decapitate the leadership in the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital looks like a city, but it comes from Latin caput, head.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing the head is decapitation, the sense of the second phrase; the first splits into two words.
